subject: Pricing Edge - p95 latency spike and immediate mitigation asks
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 29 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: [Alert] pricing-edge p95 jump to ~5s (initial observation)

Karthik,

Monitoring flagged a sustained p95 jump on pricing-edge-prod starting ~08:55 PDT. p50 marginally up, but p95 jumped from ~2.4s to ~5s over ~10 minutes. Error rate is unchanged, but tail latency is impacting ops endpoints used by EdgeRetail checkout.

What I have so far: 
- Host-level metrics look normal (no CPU/GPU saturation)
- Kernel scheduling queue shows an increased retry count on worker-threads
- Captured a lightweight heap snapshot (attached: heap-snapshot-20270529.txt) and a short perf trace

Immediate ask: can we throttle EdgeRetail's high-QPS routes to mitigate tail while we investigate kernel scheduling regressions? If so I can push a routing rule now.

Attaching: heap snapshot, brief perf notes.

-ben

--
Ben Carter
SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 29 May 2027 09:34:12 -0700
Subject: Re: [Alert] pricing-edge p95 jump to ~5s (initial observation)

Thanks Ben — good catch. Quick plan below, want product + CS alignment before we touch anything that affects customers.

Proposed immediate mitigations (short-lived):
1) Apply a per-customer QPS cap for EdgeRetail (500 qps) on pricing-edge routing to blunt tail. This is reversible and low-risk.
2) Enable conservative request batching for the pricing hot-path for 30m window (reduces scheduling pressure).
3) If tail remains high after 15m, perform a controlled rollback of the last kernel-scheduler flag we deployed last night. That rollback will require product sign-off.

Ben: can you stage the routing rule and batching toggle as config flags we can flip quickly? Attach the runbook when you have a draft.
Marissa: do we want to approve the cap vs rollback? My preference is cap-first + batching while we validate the kernel regression hypothesis.
Monica: if we cap, I'll draft a short customer note; can you review tone / escalation path?

I attached a short runbook (runbook-pricing-edge.pdf) and a customer note draft.

- Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Head of Platform Reliability, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 29 May 2027 10:05:47 -0700
Subject: Re: [Alert] pricing-edge p95 jump to ~5s (initial observation)

I can stage both changes now. Status updates:
- Routing rule: ready as "cap-edge-retail-500-qps" (will require one API call to enable)
- Batching toggle: non-disruptive (adds 20-40ms to p50, but helps tail)
- Kernel flag rollback: I can prepare the revert, but it requires a rolling restart on the pricing hot pool which will cause small amounts of in-flight request retries (we should avoid during peak).

Hypothesis: a scheduler yield path introduced last night may have increased inter-thread handoffs under certain request shapes we see from EdgeRetail (many small requests in tight bursts). If we can blunt QPS and increase batching it should drop tail latency quickly.

I'll attach a short perf trace and the heap snapshot I captured (heap-snapshot-20270529.txt).

-ben
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 29 May 2027 11:17:03 -0700
Subject: Re: [Alert] pricing-edge p95 jump to ~5s (initial observation)

Agree with cap-first approach. Product decision: do NOT rollback kernel flag right away — we should minimize restarts during EdgeRetail's midday peak (they're in US-PST).

Actionables from product: 
- Approve per-customer QPS cap for EdgeRetail at 500 qps for 2 hours.
- Approve batching toggle now (approve staging in prod for 30m window).
- If we see no improvement in 20 minutes after cap + batching, escalate to a controlled rollback during a narrow maintenance window (we'll coordinate with CS).

Monica: please review the draft customer note and confirm it is acceptable. Keep the message to a single paragraph + clear ask to retry after 15 minutes. We'll avoid technical detail.

Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Product Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: EdgeRetail Ops <ops@edgeretail.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 29 May 2027 15:47:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing edge - brief note on degraded tail latency (temporary mitigation)

Hi team — this is Karthik from Redwood Platform Reliability. We observed a temporary increase in checkout latency affecting pricing responses for a subset of requests this morning. Our SRE team applied a short-term traffic cap and conservative batching to reduce the tail while we investigate; the changes are in effect now and we expect improvements within 10–15 minutes.

What we changed: per-customer QPS cap (500 qps) + conservative batching on pricing endpoints for a 2 hour window. These are reversible and non-invasive.

If you continue to see degraded responses after 15 minutes, please reply to this thread and we will escalate immediately; otherwise no action is required on your side. Apologies for the interruption — we know checkout latency is critical and we're prioritizing a permanent fix.

Attached: short runbook for incident steps (runbook-pricing-edge.pdf).

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Platform Reliability, Redwood Inference
Karthik_Iyer@redwood.ai
